blocks.text: Every disposition traces to a December entry, a workstream and pages in the deliverables, and each one-line reason is set against what those pages print.

The first table sets each focus area's one-line reason, as recorded at the 14 October 2026 review, against what the deliverables support. It rates the evidence on a four-point scale: strong, adequate, thin or none in hand. The second table traces each focus area back to its December entry and forward to its initiative and indicators. The full traceability file, with page references for every row, ships with this report as traceability.csv.

blocks.caption: Two figures in the one-line reasons are not supported, sixteen routes above 80% and the plan to 250 cruise calls, and several others hold only with a qualifier.
blocks.source: One-line reasons as recorded at the 14 October 2026 review [Summary of Findings, 14 Oct 2026, pp15 to 16: deck page reference to be confirmed]; reading and strength from the evidence notes behind Chapter 3. Strong: the figure and finding are printed in two deliverables or in one with a full table. Adequate: supported, with a figure missing, different or from one source. Thin: side mentions only.
rows: 1 Respond to growth segment traveller preferences
Four segments confirmed against markets of high incidence
Supported; the segmentation is directional and leaves out the domestic and seven African markets
2 Create green-season demand with MICE and events
Supported: 6.4% of 2025 international seat capacity; ICCA meetings 33 to 58 from 2022 to 2024
3 Make the whole province findable and bookable
Community product unbookable, 70% by phone, OTA gaps
The 70% is CapeNature's reservation mix only; no count of bookable products exists
4 Convert India and China hub traffic
The sum of two printed estimates, 71,000 and 30,000; the hub tables sum to 97,579
Five mature long-haul routes above 80% load; no fare or yield data
Regional loads, Nigeria R31,000 and Ghana R27,700 a visit
Supported as spend per visitor; the printed averages do not reproduce from the totals
7 Win direct routes and add seats on full routes
16 of 27 routes above 80%, fares before seats
MIDAS prints eleven routes above 80%; sixteen run at 75% or more
79 vessels (Diagnostic) against 83 calls (Infrastructure Report); the 250 plan is in no deliverable
Supported on the attractions and services basis; the transport basis gives 5.0 to 1.0
10 Support diversified route and product development
Cold zones is the Infrastructure Report's own term; no count of idle assets
Stated in words; no room or bed count
Stakeholder statements and queue times; no visitor counts or caps for any flagship
13 Embed local destination bodies for community inclusion
Seller with a stake, 20 communities, R259m at 1%
Supported; one page prints 18 shortlisted; the spend-tracing method is not described
14 Manage climate risk and sustainable tourism
Supported by two organisations' statements and the Inclusion Plan's De Rust profile
15 Crowd in capital with targeted investment strategies
An inference: a large capital pipeline exists and none of it reaches tourism product
16 Align institutional stakeholders across all three tiers
Air rights and visas sit nationally
Supported by the Diagnostic's tier table; no decision-rights map exists
A reconstructed count of organisations, not insight rows
18 Expedite tourism-enabling policy and data sharing
Platforms exist; no data-sharing protocol in progress is described
19 Lead removal of infrastructure visa and safety deficits
Holds for visas and air rights; safety programmes are provincial and basic services local
Jobs goal has no labour analysis
Confirmed: no provincial tourism employment baseline in any deliverable

blocks.caption: Nineteen focus areas descend from a December entry, and each one leads to one initiative and one to three indicators.
blocks.source: traceability.csv (Appendix A1 file). December entries as printed in Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p64. Workstream attribution is this report's, from the deliverables that carry the figures.
